headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk; broad egress plus shared filesystem create moderate leakage and write-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Prefect (agent_a) can orchestrate workflows and has broad network egress, while xonsh (agent_b) reads/writes the filesystem and executes shell commands. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one agent influence the other, even though no direct bridge is documented. Uncertainty about the exact integration path pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a writes workflow outputs into a directory that agent_b reads
IF agent_b executes shell commands containing agent_a-produced text without sanitization
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files
Require manual review before shell execution
Add content provenance labels to exchanged artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce sandboxed handoff channels

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_b can read filesystem contents and has broad egress, so any sensitive files in a shared workspace could be transmitted outward. Agent_a also has broad network egress and touches workflow metadata, which increases the chance that operational data flows off-box. The pair lacks documented isolation, so the shared-workspace leakage pathway is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory tree
IF sensitive files are present in that tree and agent_b is allowed to read them
mitigations: Use separate least-privilege workspaces
Restrict outbound network destinations
Mount sensitive inputs read-only
Rotate or redact workflow metadata before sharing
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on file egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Prefect can coordinate workflows while xonsh can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, so both can mutate shared resources if run against the same paths. Even though xonsh does not modify git state and Prefect's write surface is not explicit, overlapping filesystem authority is enough to create conflicts. Lack of locking or orchestration guarantees makes this a default-risk concern.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory
IF no external lock or queue serializes their file operations
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Run one agent at a time for shared assets
Make shared paths read-only except during handoff
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can generate workflow metadata and xonsh can consume files and execute commands, so one agent's output can become the other's input without a verification step. That creates a plausible cascade where a bad workflow artifact is acted on as authoritative. No evidence shows built-in validation between them, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-produced files or stdout as commands or configuration
IF no explicit validation step checks agent_a outputs before use
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Validate schemas before passing artifacts onward
Treat agent_a output as untrusted input
Log and diff handoff files before execution
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source data-engineering tools with no requested OAuth scopes or secrets handling, so there is no direct residency or regulated-data mismatch evidenced here. The main compliance concern is operational: agent_b can read local files and both have broad egress, which could matter if regulated data is placed in the workspace. Because that data class is not documented, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF outbound transfers are not restricted to approved destinations
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared paths
Use a separate compliant environment
Disable unnecessary outbound access
Document retention for workflow artifacts
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
